What I value

Project sizes vary, but the questions I return to when deciding stay the same. Every case study traces back to one of these three.

  1. 01

    Put "why build this" into words first

    The lower a project's priority, the more its survival depends on stating its purpose in one sentence. I link the user's hesitation to a KPI before talking about features.

  2. 02

    Speed comes from removing things

    When the value of an experience is how fast it arrives, I question each step in between, including the ones teams assume they need, like a landing page.

  3. 03

    Build what stays with the team after I leave

    Tooling, design systems, KPI definitions. I count the structures that let a team repeat good decisions without me as part of the design work.

Now

UI/UX Designer at medimo since April 2026. In medical AI, I work on the screens and also on building agreement with the business side.

medimo · Team

Map the workflow in BPMN, agree on "why it matters" with KPIs

I drew the BPMN for high-priority features myself and worked with the PdM to define KPIs and outcome metrics. We use them to show the business side why each feature is needed and what it changes.

medimo · Success

Refining the product from what customers need

As part of the Success team, I learn what customers need and use it to keep raising the UI/UX of the current product.

AI × UX

Designing AI as an experience first

Prompt, UX flow, UI, trust, fallback, human handoff. Explainability, error states and privacy are part of the design from the start.
